PullRequest.Title: smoke: write {} explicitly when clearing user settings
PullRequest.Body:
Fixes the flaky `Terminal Profiles › should use the default contributed profile on panel open and for splitting` smoke test on Windows `Electron-Smoke (shard 3/3)`. It hit 2 unrelated branches in PR CI ([job 122251424555](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/actions/runs/40521963325/job/122251424555) and [job 121811263281](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/actions/runs/40390825918/job/121811263281)), timing out on `.tabs-list .monaco-list-row[data-index="1"] … .label-name` after all 4 attempts.

## What actually fails

The failure screenshot shows the split **did** happen, but both tabs are `pwsh`, not `JavaScript Debug Terminal`. The default-profile change was never applied. Right after `selectDefaultShell` → `JavaScript Debug Terminal`, the window logs:

```
Unable to write into user settings. Please open the user settings to correct errors/warnings in it and try again.
```

That happens on every attempt, because `settings.json` was already invalid JSON before the suite started.

## Why settings.json was invalid

`SettingsEditor.clearUserSettings()` selects all, deletes, then types a single `{` and relies on bracket auto-closing to add `}` (`// will auto close }`). It never checks that the brace was closed. In both failing runs, the `clearUserSettings` that runs just before Terminal Profiles is immediately followed by

```
MCP migration: Failed to parse MCP config from …/User/settings.json: SyntaxError
```

The Terminal Profiles `before` then appends its settings after the `{`, so the file stays invalid and every later settings write is refused. The passing reruns of the same shard have no such parse error.

## Fix (test automation only)

`clearUserSettings` now types `{}` and waits for the editor contents to be exactly `{}` before saving. The driver sends keyboard text one character at a time through Monaco's type interceptors, so this produces `{}` whether or not `{` auto-closes: if it does, the `}` overtypes the auto-inserted brace, and if it doesn't, it's inserted. Any other unexpected content now fails inside `clearUserSettings` instead of corrupting the next suite.

## Validation

- `tsc -p test/automation` and eslint are clean.
- **Forced-failure proof in this PR's CI** (temporary commits, now dropped), turning off `editor.autoClosingBrackets` before each `clearUserSettings`:
  - **With the fix:** every smoke, remote and browser job was green, with 0 `settings.json` parse errors ([run](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/actions/runs/40541587222)).
  - **Original `{`:** the Terminal Profiles split test failed with the CI signature on Windows shard 3/3, Windows Remote and macOS shard 1/2, with 37 parse errors and 6 `Unable to write into user settings` ([run](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/actions/runs/40544076390)).
  - Details are in [this comment](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/344594#issuecomment-6448294803).

Scenarios.Scenario: Smoke-test cleanup resets user settings to an empty JSON object between terminal suites/tests.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The reset runs synchronously in Mocha hooks: open settings, select/delete content, type the replacement, verify editor text, save settings.json, then close the editor. The added exact-content verification is on this test critical path but normally completes on its first read.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Playwright page evaluation invokes the in-window driver to insert editor text.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One typeInEditor roundtrip per reset both before and after the diff; only the payload changes from one brace to two braces.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same single automation roundtrip typed `{`; after the diff it types `{}`.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Required before the reset can verify and save the file; the extra character is handled in the same driver call and does not add boundary fan-out.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Location: test/automation/src/settings.ts:58 via Editor.waitForEditorContents, Code.waitForTextContent, and PlaywrightDriver.getElements
ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Playwright page evaluation queries and serializes the editor .view-lines element text for exact-content verification.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Normally one additional getElements roundtrip per reset; only retries at 100 ms intervals if the editor has not reached exactly `{}`, bounded at 200 attempts.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: waitForTypeInEditor already performed a content query accepting any text containing `{`; there was no subsequent exact-content query.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Adds one normally immediate DOM-query roundtrip before save. On unexpected content it deliberately blocks up to the existing 20-second polling bound and fails at the reset point rather than allowing later tests to continue with invalid settings.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Save the open settings.json file after editor content is reset.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One save per reset before and after the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The reset saved settings.json once after typing the single brace.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The save must complete before the editor closes; the diff does not add or move the filesystem write.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One reset per hook invocation. There are 11 static clearUserSettings call sites in terminal smoke tests, with a small fixed number of additional executions from per-test hooks; cost does not scale with user data because the replacement and expected text are always two characters.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: All operations are awaited sequentially. No Promise.all, queue, or cross-reset concurrency is introduced.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache participates. Both cold and warm runs perform the same automation calls; the new check is not cached and is expected to succeed immediately after the existing substring-content check.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence in the call path and one-extra-roundtrip mechanism from the changed line through waitForEditorContents to PlaywrightDriver.getElements. High confidence that it is bounded and not a reportable regression.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact Playwright roundtrip duration varies by CI host, but the added normal-path operation is one non-recursive DOM element query over a fixed two-character editor and has fixed, low cardinality. A timeout occurs only when the asserted reset invariant fails.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable performance regression. The diff adds a fixed-cost exact verification and one character to an existing automation operation; it does not fan out filesystem or process work, create concurrency, retain state, or add work to a product runtime hot path. The bounded synchronization also prevents later smoke tests from spending retries/timeouts on a malformed settings file.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over the sole changed file and all diff pages. Traced the smoke-test reset through editor typing, DOM polling, Playwright boundary calls, and settings-file save. The only added cost is one normally immediate fixed-size DOM query per reset, which is bounded, low-cardinality test synchronization and does not meet the threshold for a performance finding.
